slots.title: Trump waives Graham Act Russia sanctions
slots.body:
The White House invoked a national-interest waiver under the Graham Act to hold off new Russia-related sanctions and tariffs before they were scheduled to bite.

CNBC reports the move covers duties on Russian goods, steps aimed at major Russian energy buyers, and other restrictions—two days ahead of the law’s implementation deadline.

Same session, Brent crude settled up 3.7% at 109.86.

U.S. equity benchmarks finished lower: the S&P 500 down 1.1% to 7,659.44 and the Nasdaq Composite down 2.1% to 26,140.03.

Which part of the waiver—energy buyers vs. broader goods—matters most for your read on supply chains?

#economy #geopolitics

slots.title: Warsh silent on October Fed rates
slots.body:
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said Friday he will not prejudge rate decisions at the upcoming October and December meetings.

The comment lands as the U.S. economic calendar lists a 10:00 a.m.
ET IMF meeting entry for Oct. 17.

The 10-year Treasury yield in the latest FMP snapshot (Oct. 15) stood at 5.1%.

The 2-year minus 10-year spread was 0.33 percentage point—short rates still below the 10-year by that margin.

MarketWatch separately framed this month’s Fed decision as a closer call than pricing implies; Warsh did not tip either way in the Fast Company report.

What would you need to see in the next data print to map October vs. December?

#Fed #rates

slots.title: Fed call “closer” than markets price
slots.body:
MarketWatch on Oct. 17: this month’s Fed interest-rate decision is a closer call than markets think.

The piece lays out arguments against a rate hike and where some economists push back—without resolving the split.

Latest Treasury snapshot in the feed (Oct. 15): 1-year at 4.5%, 2-year at 4.8%, 10-year at 5.1%.

The S&P 500 closed Oct. 17 at 7,659.44, down 1.1% on the session.

The CBOE Volatility Index finished at 19.99, up 21.4% from the prior close of 16.46.

Seeking Alpha’s week-in-review note also cited hotter-than-expected CPI still in the rearview alongside bank earnings—context readers were already weighing into the weekend.

Where do you land: hike, hold, or cut—and what single input drives that view?

#macro #Fed

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 17, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 closed at 7,659.44, down 84.62 points (−1.1%), after trading between 7,631.77 and 7,756.84.

The Nasdaq Composite finished at 26,140.03, down 572.99 (−2.1%), with a session low of 26,023.10.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended at 52,002.41, down 175.28 (−0.3%) — a milder decline than the growth benchmarks.

The Russell 2000 closed at 2,721.37, down 45.90 (−1.7%).

The CBOE Volatility Index settled at 19.99, up 3.53 (+21.4%), with an intraday high of 22.31.

Headlines around the close described an AI-linked selloff on the Nasdaq and chip pressure; MarketWatch noted the S&P 500 tech sector’s worst week in about a year and a half while broader average-stock measures fared relatively better over the week.

Mega-cap tech and platforms closed lower: $META −3.7% to 709.33, $GOOGL −2.5% to 340.59, $GOOG −2.3% to 336.91, $TSLA −2.1% to 354.72, $MSFT −1.9% to 529.05, and $AMZN −1.9% to 250.00.

Software and media also weakened: $ORCL −4.6% to 128.22 and $NFLX −2.9% to 70.53.

Semiconductor and chip-adjacent names declined: $AVGO −4.5% to 328.75, $INTC −5.8% to 89.85, $TSM −2.3% to 412.61, and $NVDA −1.4% to 214.13.

$AAPL bucked the megacap tech trend, up 0.4% to 343.46, with a day high of 347.82 against a 52-week high of 348.15 in the quote data.

Defensive and consumer staples names were firmer:
- $PEP +2.4% to 131.49
- $KO +2.1% to 93.90
- $JNJ +0.9% to 255.56

Financials showed mixed large-cap results: $JPM +1.2% to 339.72 while $UNH −1.3% to 401.43.

Energy equities rose with oil: $XOM +2.5% to 178.98 as Brent crude settled at 109.86 (+3.7%) and gold futures at 4,181.10 (+0.3%).

The injected Treasury snapshot (dated 2026-10-15) showed the 10-year yield at 5.1% and a 2s10s spread of 0.33 percentage points.

Cross-asset moves at the close included the U.S. dollar proxy $UUP −0.3% to 28.92, Bitcoin at 81,722.58 (+0.4%), and overseas indexes mixed earlier in the cycle (Nikkei 225 +1.4%, FTSE 100 +0.4%, Hang Seng −0.5%).

The U.S. economic calendar listed a low-impact IMF Meeting on Oct. 17; no earnings entries appeared in the injected earnings calendar for this bundle.
